Branch

Leadership

A ladder by capacity

Service, advocacy and professional life. People enter at Emerging Leaders and move by what they are ready to take on, not by age. The order is a suggestion, never a prerequisite.

Programmes on this branch

Emerging Leaders Summit

The entry rung of the Leadership branch. afrp.org has no page for it, and the record states nothing beyond its age band and its place on the branch.

Plan only other
Ramallah Business & Professional Network

A network for members in business and the professions: training courses, mentoring, networking events and a mixer at the Convention. It holds one voting seat on the AFRP Board.

Built Flagship other
Congressional Outreach

Year-round advocacy for Palestinian rights at every level of government and across party lines: members meet their own elected officials, and the committee briefs State Department and DHS officials.

Plan only Committee
Day of Action

A yearly advocacy summit on Capitol Hill: members meet their representatives and senators and attend advocacy-tools sessions with partner organisations.

Plan only other
Educational & Cultural Exchange Mission

Missions to Ramallah since 2015 for American journalists, educators, clergy and political leaders, plus graduate-student delegations, fellowships and cultural programming.

Plan only Cohort

How people move along it

A ladder by capacity. Entry is at Emerging Leaders. People move by what they are ready to take on, and the order is a suggestion, never a prerequisite. Inside every programme, people move through the same five rungs: hear · show up · take part · give or serve · lead (D25).

Outcomes this branch reports

  • How many Exchange Mission alumni join Congressional Outreach or the Day of Action
  • How many RBPN members give or serve in another programme
  • How many people reach the Lead rung and hold a committee seat

How outcomes are measured for each branch is itself an open question (Q-19).
